comments.author: @HolgerRuneFan
comments.text:
This is a wonderful documentary with a fabulous narrator. I'm a native Californian who drives 1300+ miles (one way) every May and October to visit Montana. I've done it since the 1980's. But what this documentary doesn't show is that outsiders are not really welcomed in Montana. Despite the fact I love this state passionately, the moment locals see my California license plate, I am shunned, treated poorly and sometimes even verbally attacked. 

Montana is insular and simply don't accept or embrace any non-local. I can't imagine how I would be treated if I moved there despite sharing their conservative outlook and loving the state with all my heart.

comments.text: For those who live in Maui, what’s the one thing tourists completely misunderstand about everyday life there?

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: That’s a great question. I think many visitors see Maui mainly as a paradise vacation destination, while everyday life there is much more complex — with high living costs, limited housing, long commutes in some areas, and a strong local culture that deserves respect.
